record_type: Published investigation episode index; not original organizational data
unit: Requests for additional on-orbit imagery and their cancellation, January21–22,2003; not the entire accident
roles: Debris Assessment Team and engineering management
Mission Management Team chair and mission operations
NASA/Department of Defense liaisons and imaging-resource planners

reported_steps.evidence_form: Board narrative plus reproduced co-chair email
reported_steps.description: Assessment team supported seeking additional imagery to reduce uncertainty and routed its request through engineering.
Contacts described as information gathering initiated resource planning; distinct requests must not be collapsed into a single approved workflow.

reported_steps.evidence_form: Reported cancellation plus Board's likely reconstruction
reported_steps.description: Liaison cancelled the request. Board reconstructs management checking for an official requirement without asking the assessment team directly.

reported_steps.evidence_form: Board narrative, obtained personal notes and log entry
reported_steps.description: Schedule/resource and perceived utility concerns appear in the account; Board reports image-quality, difficulty and cost were not established with capability holders.

reported_outcome: The imagery action was halted; the Board summary at166–167 records the requests and missed opportunities. No counterfactual safety outcome is estimated here.
timing_qualification: The report says initiation and rescission occurred within90minutes; the intervening management sequence is explicitly described as likely, not a complete independently timed event log.

evidence_layers.contemporaneous_records_reproduced: Emails/logs reprinted inside the report, not separately authenticated raw files
evidence_layers.investigation_reconstruction: Board chronology and its likely-sequence qualification
evidence_layers.board_interpretation: Routing shaped how the request was treated; capability/cost knowledge was limited
evidence_layers.this_project_inference: Information acquisition can itself require sponsorship/authorization; recording an information gap does not diagnose a representation-only remedy

known_unknowns: Complete receipt and shared understanding by every decision-maker
Actual available image resolution, costs and operational disruption for this request
Separate effects of route, priority, expertise, interpretation and authority
Whether a differently routed request would have been approved
Whether additional images would have changed mission decisions or the outcome
comparison_classification: Authority/requirement and evidence-acquisition contrast; not proof of complete common understanding without coordination
proposed_observation_fields: Who requests it and through which route
Who can recognize a requirement or authorize acquisition
What action occurred and what remains unknown
